statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6 (low) sits well below the block threshold after NQ recovered the full 236 points from its 29,274.75 overnight low and returned above Friday's 29,491.75 settlement, while Stress 38 (moderate) reflects Brent above $90, September rate-hike odds near 59-60% after the Jackson Hole remarks, and a month-end session that opens payrolls week.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-14:30 UTC, where the U.S. cash open on the final August session meets month-end rebalancing and the first deep-liquidity pricing of both the weekend Larak Island exchange and the hawkish Fed repricing. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: the overnight geopolitical shock is fully retraced as NQ reclaims Friday's settlement, while $90 Brent and September hike odds near 60% keep Stress moderate
body: The retracement is complete. The Nasdaq-100 September contract trades 29,510.75, up 19.00 points or 0.06% against Friday's 29,491.75 settlement, inside an overnight range of 29,274.75 to 29,545.50. The low at 29,274.75 was printed around the 00:00 UTC hour after the United States struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iran's Revolutionary Guards answered with missiles at American bases in Jordan, eight of which Jordanian air defences intercepted without casualties. That low has now held roughly six hours and price has recovered the entire 236-point decline. Orderly two-way discovery with a completed retracement is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the tail measure is built to detect, so Tail eases from 8 to 6. S&P 500 futures at 7,707.50, down 0.19%, show the same broadly flat shape. The stress backdrop remains real. Brent trades $90.53, up 2.76%, and WTI $85.53, up 2.56%, carrying a Hormuz risk premium; reporting notes that roughly six to eight million barrels a day still transit the strait and that traders increasingly frame the situation in economic rather than imminent-supply terms, which argues against treating this as a discontinuity. The rates picture is the second driver: after the hawkish Jackson Hole remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, futures markets price roughly a 59 to 60 percent chance of a September rate increase against about 35 percent on Thursday. The Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 2-year near 4.20 percent and the 10-year near 4.67 percent at the latest published daily observation, with the 2-year reported to have traded as high as 4.32 percent intraday on the repricing. Cross-asset alignment is therefore incomplete: equities have retraced back to unchanged while oil is bid and yields are broadly steady, which supports Stress at 38 rather than any increase in Tail. Cboe's VIX last closed at 14.43, a subdued level that is a Friday cash print rather than live evidence. The shared Finviz context file is roughly 290 minutes old, well past its 90-minute freshness limit, so it was treated as stale and excluded from the evidence base; every level above comes from independent primary-source research. The day's structure is defined by the 13:30 UTC cash open on the final August session, where month-end rebalancing meets the first deep-liquidity pricing of the weekend escalation, and by the 20:00 UTC close where that rebalancing settles. Neither is an automatic block: both are checkpoints at which observed opening structure, not anticipation, would justify a higher tail reading. The week then runs into ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP and the Beige Book on Wednesday, ISM Services and jobless claims on Thursday, and August payrolls on Friday.

lookbackSummary: Across the previous 24 hourly assessments Tail ran at 5 through the whole of Friday's aftermath and the quiet Sunday session, then stepped to 9 and peaked at 15 in the 00:00 UTC hour as the Larak Island exchange drove NQ to 29,274.75. Stress rose in parallel from 25 to a high of 44. Every hour since has walked Tail back - 13, 11, 10, 10, 8 - as the overnight low held and price retraced, and dominant mode moved from trend-down through mixed. No hour reached the watch threshold and the mapped state stayed EA_ON throughout.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is continued two-way trade with Tail held in the 6 to 13 band and no hour reaching the 20 watch threshold, so the mapped state remains EA_ON across the window. Two narrow checkpoints carry the elevated conditional readings: the 13:30 UTC cash open on the final August session, where month-end rebalancing meets the first deep-liquidity pricing of the weekend escalation, and the 19:00 UTC hour into the 20:00 UTC close where that rebalancing settles. Stress peaks near 47 around the open and decays to the mid-30s overnight, while Confidence falls from 86 to 70 with distance from observed evidence. The reading would be invalidated by a decisive loss of the 29,274.75 overnight low, by repeated extension after failed retracements, or by an oil-led leg that pulls yields and index futures into alignment.
